title_original: Jeff Bezos says he was “heavily involved” in choosing James Bond; reveals casting process
excerpt_original: The Amazon CEO also revealed that it was down to five finalists, who all screen-tested.

blocks.text: Amazon CEO Jeff Bezos said he was “heavily involved” in choosing the actor to play the next James Bond, which was revealed as Robert Pattinson on Monday (November 16).

“We ran a really tight process,” Bezos said while speaking at the Semafor Silicon Valley & The World Event in California. “There was a big group initially and we down-selected to five finalists, and then we did real, old-fashioned screen tests.”
The other four finalists were understood to be Josh O’Connor, Nicholas Hoult, Jack Lowden and Callum Turner.
Bezos explained the screen tests consisted of three different scenes and involved costumes, sets and other actors. The decision to cast Pattinson was made on Friday (November 13).
“By the time we get to this list of five finalists, they were all amazing but there was something special about Rob Pattinson and his performances,” the Amazon CEO continued.
“It was universal, kind of immediately undebated. Denis [Villeneuve], the director, we all gravitated towards Rob.”

Bezos admitted that they were “initially biased against” Pattinson due to his level of fame. “We thought we should have someone a little more unknown,” he explained. “But in the screening tests, it was so obvious. He is James Bond.”

This will be the first James Bond film under the creative control of Amazon MGM, after the company bought the rights from Eon Productions in February 2025 at a reported cost of $1bn. Producers are Amy Pascal and David Heyman for their Pascal Pictures and Heyday Films, respectively. Steven Knight is writing the screenplay.
